description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/examples/htgr_sim_v1.

SYMPTOM. TampinesSteamArray::set_inlet_enthalpy() has no effect on the solution. With a UNIFORM initial field the enthalpy field is bit-identical after 30000 step() calls, in BOTH directions:
  seed 523.15 K (he 1085.7 kJ/kg), inlet BC 168.7 kJ/kg -> he[0..8] all 1085.7 kJ/kg
  seed 523.15 K (he 1085.7 kJ/kg), inlet BC 3000.0 kJ/kg -> he[0..8] all 1085.7 kJ/kg
Setup: n=8, L=4 m, A=0.02 m2, p=4 MPa, set_pimple_algorithm(3,2,0.3,0.3), set_uniform_velocity_field(0.17 m/s), set_inlet_velocity(0.17 m/s), set_outlet_pressure(4 MPa), re-applied every step. 30 s simulated = ~1.3 tube transits.

NOT A TIMESTEP ISSUE. Swept dt = 1e-4, 5e-4, 2e-3, 6.25e-3, 1.25e-2 s, each for 30 s of simulated time (up to 300000 steps). Identical no-op at every dt. ~0.35 ms/step throughout.

CONVECTION ITSELF WORKS. Seeding a NON-uniform single-phase profile (cells 0-1 at 500 K, rest 400 K) and running at 0.17 m/s DOES advect the slug downstream (step 10000: peak at cells 2-3; step 20000: peak at cells 5-6). So the convection operator is live; it is specifically the inlet PATCH enthalpy that is not entering the energy equation. Consistent with the uniform-field result: a uniform field has zero internal convective change, so if the boundary term is ignored, nothing moves at all.

Also in that slug run, cell 0 relaxes to the BACKGROUND value (~401 K) rather than to the 500 K inlet BC, and downstream cells dip to 347 K, BELOW anything seeded -- so the boundary appears to contribute an unset/zero enthalpy rather than the value passed in.

CONTRAST: OPCPFluidArray (outram-park-fork-coolprop) DOES respond to the identical call sequence -- seeded 523.15 K, inlet BC 5067.6 kJ/kg (973 K helium), he[0] moved 2731.5 -> 3774.0 kJ/kg and the array reaches ~971 K uniform given enough simulated time. So the two sibling rhoPimpleFoam ports differ here; OPCP is the reference behaviour.

RELATED DEAD ENDS (both blocked for a boiling stream):
- writing he.internal[0] directly each step PANICS: 't,p flashing at eqm out of bounds!'
- set_temperature_vector() does a (p,T) flash, which panics on two-phase input, so it cannot impose a subcooled inlet on an array whose other cells are in the dome.

IMPACT. Blocks the 3-stream counter-flow steam generator (OPCPFluidArray <-> SolidColumn <-> TampinesSteamArray) for htgr_sim_v1 and fhr_sim_v2: the cold side cannot be given a feedwater inlet, so it has no axial temperature profile and the exchanger cannot be driven. Note fhr_sim_v2's existing use and the crate's own steam_generator_tube_boils_feedwater test both heat the array via lateral_link_new_power_vector and initialise it AT the inlet state, so neither exercises this path -- which is why it has gone unnoticed.
title: TampinesSteamArray: set_inlet_enthalpy is ignored by the energy equation (blocks any advection-driven inlet)

acceptance_criteria: The intended reading of 'the mapping' is settled by the maintainer, a CPU baseline is measured for it, and the wgpu decision is made on that measurement rather than on expectation.
description:
Maintainer raised this at 02:30 SGT, OUTSIDE active working hours, so it is RECORDED HERE UNANSWERED rather than analysed. Answer it in a working window.

THE QUESTION AS ASKED: 'I suppose the mapping is where wgpu may pay off?'

'The mapping' is ambiguous in context and the reading must be settled before any analysis. At least three candidates, all live in this workspace:

  (a) PROPERTY-TABLE MAPPING (state -> properties), batch. Immediately preceding context was CoolProp tabular backends (op-id3l.2). Upstream CoolProp 8.0's fast_evaluate is explicitly a cache-bypassing, allocation-free BATCH API writing into a caller-allocated buffer - which is already the GPU-shaped workload. Per-cell property evaluation over a mesh is embarrassingly parallel.

  (b) CROSS-MESH MAPPING (meshToMesh / RBF non-conformal) in genfoam multi_region - 3,953 lines / 24 tests already implemented.

  (c) MGXS rung 2->3 SEAM (op-fhjn): GeN-Foam nuclearData is parameterised by feedback variables via polyharmonic-spline RBF interpolation across perturbed reactor states. That is a scattered-data interpolation mapping.

WHAT IS ALREADY GPU-CAPABLE (verified 2026-08-13, wgpu in 7 crate manifests): boon-lay, njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-blender, outram-foam-basic-lib, outram-mc-libs, outram-park-fork-pflotran, raffles. So the question is not 'can we' but 'which mapping is actually the bottleneck'.

DO NOT GUESS THE ANSWER. The workspace rule is profile-first, and op-id3l.2's acceptance already requires measuring per-call overhead before choosing an implementation. Any wgpu claim here needs a measured CPU baseline first, and the f32-GPU / f64-CPU precision tradeoff applies as it does everywhere else in this workspace.
title: HTGR OPEN QUESTION (maintainer, 2026-08-13): is 'the mapping' where wgpu pays off?

description: Unit annotations written bare as [m] / [m^2] / [m^3] / [degrees] in doc comments are parsed by rustdoc as broken markdown links. Fixed in outram-foam-mesh on 2026-08-07 (73 replacements across 8 files, rustdoc warnings 59 -> 5) by converting to the code-span form that the crate's newer files already use. The same defect remains in ~11 other crates, ~41 sites: outram-foam-basic-lib (15), outram-foam-turbulence-lib (9), tampines-steam-tables (4), outram-foam-appbuilder-lib (4), plus dwsim-libs, coolprop, pflotran, offbeat, moltres, multiphase, bedok. Mechanical fix, good single-agent sweep. Units MUST be preserved in the text -- the human-interface rule requires units spelled out even when uom-typed.
title: workspace: bare [m] unit annotations break rustdoc in 11 crates (~41 sites)
